name: square-coil
why: An authored section wound on a helix, left-handed, against the tube formula: a 2 mm square on a radius-10, pitch-5 helix for 2.75 turns is 4 * 2.75 * sqrt((20 pi)^2 + 25) = 693.335 mm3; the exact B-rep reads 693.3357 through BRepGProp. The Frenet frame of a helix is its screw motion, so the square keeps its attitude to the axis: four B-spline walls, two flat ends, and a size no wider than the square's corner reaches (11.0003 mm). The implicit half refuses by name. The mesher's triangle count on the B-spline walls is held to 15%: GCC on x86_64 lays 9.8% more.
